extracted.intended_audience: brands, agencies, talent and creators submitting work to the Entertainment Lions (Cannes Lions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and category definitions for submitting branded entertainment work to the Entertainment Lions, including judging weightings, category-specific requirements (lengths, formats), and the standards by which work will be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall judging weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 30% creative idea; 20% strategy & insight; 30% craft & execution; 20% results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentages indicate the relative importance of each dimension when judging entries across the Entertainment categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary creative standard (unskippable/captivating)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should demonstrate ideas that are unskippable. It should captivate in order to cut through, communicating a brand message or connecting with consumers in a new way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are expected to grab audience attention and create meaningful brand connection; judges will assess whether the idea makes the work impossible to ignore and whether it delivers a clear brand link or new connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Brands' for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands refers to talent, artists, creators, influencers, streamers, athletes, teams, organisations, sponsors, platforms, media owners, rights holders or any entity that produces and distributes products and content related to the entertainment industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who can be considered the brand/entrant for the purpose of category entry and judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry relevance and multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no overall limit to how many times the same piece of work can be entered into Entertainment as long as the categories chosen are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may be entered into multiple relevant categories but entrants should ensure category choice fits the nature of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtitles recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtitles are highly recommended on all case films, films, demo films and original content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing subtitles is advised to improve accessibility and comprehension for judges and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branded Content — general definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative content crafted to build awareness for a brand by associating it with culture and values through entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries in Branded Content should show how entertainment content builds brand awareness and cultural association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction Film (Up to 5 minutes) — A01
rubrics_metrics.description: Branded fiction films or series created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. Up to 5 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Fiction Film (Up to 5 minutes) — A02
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual film, series or documentary/reality film created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. Up to 5 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction Film (5–30 minutes) — A03
rubrics_metrics.description: Branded fiction films or series created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. 5–30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Fiction Film (5–30 minutes) — A04
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual film, series or documentary/reality film created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. 5–30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction Film (Over 30 minutes) — A05
rubrics_metrics.description: Branded fiction films or series created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. Over 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Fiction Film (Over 30 minutes) — A06
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual film, series or documentary/reality film created for cinema, TV, online or video-on-demand platforms. Over 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If you're submitting a series, please upload all episodes in a single video file with slates denoting the start of the next episode. Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast / Live Streaming submission requirement — A07
rubrics_metrics.description: Cinema, TV or online live content, including live coverage of events and use of live streaming platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * Please provide a sample film file of up to 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio Content — A08
rubrics_metrics.description: Content created for radio, podcasts or other audio platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should reflect creative use of purely audio formats to build brand connection through entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand Integration — A09
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of brands into existing content such as films, documentaries, series, live streams, TV or audio/radio shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging will consider how naturally and effectively the brand is integrated into existing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional Content for Publishers & Networks — A10
rubrics_metrics.description: Original content/programming created to promote a media company, network, broadcaster or publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work will be judged not just on the content, but also on how it communicated or evolved the identity of the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Entertainment — B01
rubrics_metrics.description: Live entertainment, including concerts, live streams, stunts and festivals held physically or within virtual worlds, crafted to amplify a brand’s message and increase engagement with an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate how live elements amplified the brand message and drove audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Realities & Emerging Tech — B02
rubrics_metrics.description: Immersive experiences that creatively push the boundaries of technology within entertainment. This could include, but not be limited to, AR, VR, XR, voice technology, blockchain technology, gamification, virtual worlds, the metaverse and all other emerging platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology; entries should be realized experiences that push tech creatively within entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 360 Integrated Brand Experience — B03
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiences that successfully carry a brand’s message across multiple platforms/channels, both online and offline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how content featuring a brand’s message, product or service has been seamlessly implemented on various platforms to continue and amplify meaningful consumers’ experience and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Engagement / Distribution Strategy — C01
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience engagement and distribution strategies that creatively and effectively further the content’s reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging focuses on the creativity and effectiveness of strategies used to grow reach and engage audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer & Co-Creation — C02
rubrics_metrics.description: The creative and innovative use of content creators, streamers and/or influencers to drive a brand’s message and engage with a specific audience through entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include, but is not limited to, collaborations, sponsored content and user-generated content; judges will look for originality and effectiveness of partnerships with creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand Partnerships, Sponsorships & Collaborations — D01
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic brand partnerships and collaborations that leverage branded content and entertainment to meet specific business goals and mutually benefit everyone involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging will assess strategic fit, outcomes and mutual benefit across partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with Talent — D02
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic partnerships between a brand and a talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work will be judged on how effective and mutually beneficial the partnership was.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity & Inclusion in Entertainment — E01
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand-led creative work that tackles and confronts disparities based on sex, sexuality, disability, age, race, ethnicity, origin, religion or other status within the entertainment industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should show meaningful action or creative approaches that address disparities in the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in Branded Content — E02
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground-breaking and unparalleled branded content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will reward originality and work that sets new standards in branded entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenger Brand — E03
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for tactical creativity and strategic responses that helped the brand punch above its weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Behaviour — E04
rubrics_metrics.description: Work inspired by a specific audience or community, relying on identifiable social behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how leveraging insights into consumer behaviour can create a powerful connection with a brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Humour — E05
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that celebrates the art of humour in branded communications. Infusing wit, satire, and cleverness into campaigns that provide amusement and create memorable, laughter-inducing connections with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will assess effectiveness of humour in service of the brand message and audience connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural Engagement — E06
rubrics_metrics.description: Work crafted around strategic solutions rooted in the lived experiences of culturally grounded communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work which reflects and translates the nuances of customs, behaviours, and traditions that shape foundational perspectives on identity (e.g. disability, gender, race, orientation, age). Such insights reveal how audiences choose brands and media experiences, driving growth and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category selection guidance (traditional film advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional film advertising should be entered into the Film Lions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should ensure that traditional film ads are submitted to the Film Lions rather than Entertainment categories; many Branded Content film subcategories reiterate this guidance.
